To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of S100A8 and S100A9 are not limited to the myeloid lineage and that the effects of the S100 proteins on myeloid cells are cell type–specific.
S100A9, which is constitutively present in bone marrow– derived cells, differentially regulates the phenotype of neutrophils and dendritic cells but has little effect on macrophages.

S100A9 modulates inflammatory phenotypes in different myeloid cells, and this modulation is likely to contribute in a cell type– and stage of disease–dependent manner to atherosclerosis, obesity, and related inflammatory conditions
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of S100A8 and S100A9, two members of the S100 calcium-binding protein family, in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis, obesity, and insulin resistance.
the role of S100A proteins in inflammation.
the molecular mechanisms underlying atherosclerosis and the development of obesity and insulin resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of S100a9 deficiency on atherogenesis is dependent on the cell type in which S100a9 is expressed.
S100A9 has no role in atherosclerosis or insulin resistance.
the effect of S100 A9 deficiency on atherogenesis and insulin resistance is cell-type dependent and that S100A9 may also be expressed in nonmyeliod cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S100A9 has an important function as an amplifier of inflammation.
S100A9 has a complex effect on inflammation, depending on the cell type and stage of disease progression.
S100A9 does not affect atherosclerosis and adipose tissue inflammation in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of S100A8 and S100A9, and probably other S100 proteins as well, in inflammatory conditions such as atherosclerosis and obesity is likely to be cell-type specific.
S100A9 has a very different role in different cells.
S100A9 plays a critical role in regulating the phenotype and function of dendritic cells, neutrophils and macrophages, all of which are important cell types in atherosclerosis.
